gen-dafont-eraser-fs-public-sans: Understated but commanding, Eraser draws smooth, tube-like bold letters. Public Sans follows with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, doing the quiet, trustworthy work of carrying the text while the heading makes the statement.
gen-dafont-eraser-general-sans: Chunky tubes up top, then a tall, smooth sans below. Eraser keeps every stroke bold and unvarying, while General Sans fills the line with a high x-height and curves that glide without a snag.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-hepta-slab: Eraser's bold strokes never thicken or thin, giving it a bent-wire sturdiness. And Hepta Slab, a dignified serif with open counters and stretched-out words, lets a long stretch of text breathe and feel bookish.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-padyakke-expanded-o: Eraser is all bold, uniform strokes with no thick-thin shifts. Padyakke Expanded One, a text serif, spreads its wide-mouthed letters across the line, so a long passage feels slow, literary and quietly authoritative.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-stint-ultra-expande: Eraser's bold letters keep one unvarying stroke from end to end. Stint Ultra Expanded, a serif, lets each character float apart with open counters, so the two sit together as dense weight above and traditional spaciousness below.
gen-dafont-eraser-manrope: Eraser leads with understated, bold strokes. Manrope, a sans with bright open curves and a minimal step from capitals to lowercase, keeps a longer passage approachable and smooth, its single line width carrying you along.
gen-dafont-eraser-satoshi: Satoshi brings a soaring x-height and a wide e that never pinches. Make Eraser's heading small or Satoshi's text large and that height gap between them shrinks, so keep the bold heading plainly in charge.
gen-dafont-eraser-switzer: Wiry, tubular Switzer letters stand tall with c tips that never close in, a Swiss-minded plain sans with a high waist line. Eraser is the one that makes a bold statement; Switzer does the patient explaining.
gen-dafont-eraser-work-sans: Work Sans brings a contemporary feel, with a high mean line, joins as sturdy as its strokes, and c tips held well apart. And Eraser, bold and uniform in line, sits above it as the lower, understated voice.
